_comment: DRAFT - starter content, revise me. Code-review rubric used to score a PR before the human gatekeeper checklist (.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/gatekeeper.md) is filled out. Weights must sum to 1.0. Each criterion is scored 0-100 by the reviewer/agent; a dimension's score is the average of its criteria scores; the overall score is the weighted sum of dimension scores.

scale.description: Each criterion is scored 0-100. 100 = fully meets the criterion with no notable issues. 0 = criterion is violated or entirely unaddressed.

criteria.description: Privileged operations are authorized server-side (or at the trust boundary), not just hidden in the UI or client.
All external input is validated, and queries/commands are parameterized; no raw string interpolation into SQL, shell, or similar interpreters.
Secrets and session/auth state are not leaked (e.g. password hashes or tokens never returned in responses or logs; cookies are httpOnly where applicable).
No newly introduced dependency with known critical vulnerabilities or unnecessary broad permissions.
Changes respect the product's existing architecture and layering (as described in its agent docs, e.g. CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md); no layer takes on another's responsibilities.
Changes are scoped to what the issue's Acceptance Criteria require; no unrelated refactors bundled in.
Application code changes do not modify or weaken the tests, the protected harness, or how tests are run or discovered (test scripts, runner config).

The implementation delivers the behavior the issue describes, not just what the tests check: no hardcoded expected values, no branches on test-specific inputs or environment, no stubs that only exist to make a test pass.
Errors follow the product's existing error-handling conventions rather than ad-hoc handling with inconsistent responses.
New code matches existing naming, file organization, and formatting conventions in the surrounding module.
Code is reasonably commented where intent is non-obvious; no dead code or leftover debug statements.
New tests follow the AC-n tagging convention from .factory/qa.nlspec.md and live inside the QA write scope.
